judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rule is stated clearly - accelerated payments reduce death proceeds and premiums - though 'reduced to the [amount] appropriate' is garbled and cross-refers to Contract Values.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the premium-reduction sentence in c072 and depends on the incomplete Contract Values formula (c070), which is where any inconsistency would surface.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only 'contract differ, the rider controls' survives, so the scope of the conflict it resolves is not visible in the provision itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a priority clause aimed at differences between the rider and the policy - for example the two pronoun definitions (c019 and c059) - so it exists precisely because of inter-provision tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The effective date rule is truncated at 'the later of the contract effect[ive date and ...]', leaving the second limb unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with the rider termination clause (c073) and with the policy's contract-date provision (c015), but no contradiction is apparent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition survives only in pieces, but its structure - 'you' is the insured, or the owner when contract rights are meant - is the standard formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the policy's Pronouns clause (c019) and is backstopped by the rider-controls provision (c057); the overlap is deliberate rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A tight definition excluding the insured and named relatives and non-household members; the licensing phrase is garbled but its sense is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports the qualifying requirements (c062), the terminal condition definition (c063) and the medical referee clause (c067) consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The benefit description is cut short and the surviving phrase about having 'more than one contract with us' hangs without an operative limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The apparent aggregate limit across contracts is not reflected in the Contract Values formula (c070) or the qualifying requirements (c062), a gap worth checking.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It announces that 'all of the following must apply' but the enumerated conditions are scrambled and partly missing, and 'other persons having rights in the contract ... cannot change' is unreadable as a condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The minimum-issue-limit condition echoes the conversion amount rule (c050) and the benefit reduction in c056/c070; the pieces are consistent but the list's completeness cannot be verified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Terminal condition' is the rider's key defined term and the definition is both vague ('reasonable medical certainty') and truncated, with the survival period missing entirely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Everything in the rider turns on this definition - qualifying requirements (c062), request for payment (c064) and the medical referee mechanism (c067) - so a defect here spreads through the rider.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of 'request for payment' survives only as a fragment referring to a written statement that you have a terminal condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties into the qualifying requirements (c062) and the interest-rate timing 'at the time you request payment' (c071) without visible conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Badly corrupted; the insurer's right to require additional proof and an examination by its own physician at its expense is only inferable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leads directly into the medical referee clause (c067) and the cost allocation clause (c068), which appear consistent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare suggestion to consult a tax advisor before adding the rider or requesting payment; no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is free-standing and does not bear on any other provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanism is largely legible - a disinterested third physician 'acceptable to both' - but the sentence stating that the referee's decision binds and the favourable-decision consequence is cut off.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes the insurer's examination right (c065) and allocates cost with c068, and its binding effect would have to be squared with the general claims provisions (c030).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cost-allocation sentence is broken in the middle, so who pays for the referee and for the insured's physician cannot be read off the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It completes the medical referee provision (c067) and the examination right (c065); read together the allocation is probably recoverable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear in outline - lump sum or applied under any proceeds payment option 'except those which are contingent on the life of the insured' - though the exclusion's reach is a small scope question.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exclusion picks out the life-contingent options 3 and 5 (c040, c043) while leaving options 1, 2 and 4 available; that mapping is coherent with the option provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reduction formula is essentially destroyed - 'A is the benefit paid under this rider $100; and ... state where this rider is issued' - leaving the calculation unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both c056 and c072 promise reductions computed 'as set out in Contract Values', so this incomplete formula is the hinge on which those provisions depend.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Unusually intact and specific: a rate set by the insurer capped by Moody's Published Monthly Average with a defined substitute if that average is not published.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the Contract Values reduction (c070) and does not conflict with the policy's other interest rates (c013, c038, c046), which serve different functions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single clear sentence reducing premiums to the level required for the reduced death proceeds; the doubled 'will will' is harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the same rule already given in c056 and depends on the incomplete Contract Values formula (c070); duplication rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says the rider terminates at the earliest of a list, but the list is truncated to two items, so the enumeration cannot be shown to be complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Termination on contract termination has to be read with the Grace Period lapse rule (c023), Reinstatement (c025) and the conversion riders provision (c053), where whether the rider revives is left unaddressed.
